8	/-!
9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
14	CERT-Σ-gated.
15	
16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
19	
20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
23	
24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
29	
30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
31	
32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
37	
38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
42	
43	## Main declarations
44	
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
57	  this route.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
60	-/
61

77	/-! ## The necessary direction: an open immersion of presheaves is a monomorphism
78	
79	Stated first, because it is what tells us the criterion below asks for the right thing. -/
80	
81	/-- **An open immersion of presheaves out of a representable is a monomorphism.**
82	
83	This is mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `P := IsOpenImmersion`, whose hypothesis
84	`IsOpenImmersion ≤ monomorphisms Scheme` is the landed `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.
85	
86	Recorded because the whole chart layer rests on the sentence "the Abel map is not a
87	monomorphism, so `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is false for the unrestricted divisor scheme"
88	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, repeated in `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`).  That sentence is a
89	*derivation*, not an independent input, and this lemma is the derivation. -/
90	theorem mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
92	    Mono f :=
93	  MorphismProperty.presheaf_mono_of_le IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms hf
94	
95	/-- **The elementwise form of the necessary direction**: if `f` is an open immersion of
96	presheaves then on every test it is injective on points.
97	
98	This is the clause `ChartFibrePresented.fibre_injective` below, read backwards, and it is
99	why that clause is not an artefact of this particular route: any proof of
100	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` whatsoever yields it.  For the Abel chart it is exactly "the
101	normalized effective representative is unique", i.e. the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 — so
102	GAP-2 is *forced* by the target, not merely sufficient for it. -/
103	theorem injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
104	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
105	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
106	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
107	  (mono_iff_injective (f.app T)).mp
108	    ((NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app f).mp (mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf) T)
109	
110	/-! ## The sufficient direction: the elementwise datum, and the criterion -/
111	
112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
114	
115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
118	
119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
202	    inferInstance⟩
203	
204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
205	
206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
209	
210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
211	
212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied
214	for the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`
215	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the
216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
217	
218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
221	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
223	        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
224	  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
225	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩
226	
227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
228	elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
238	
239	end
240	
241	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
17	fibre is a single point.
18	
19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
21	
22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
23	
24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
26	
27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
39	
40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
43	
44	## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one
45	
46	The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
47	wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative
48	representability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each
49	represented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the
50	second only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one
51	unconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.
52	
53	That split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from
54	elementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,
55	reducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a
56	*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.
57	Read `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
62	  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at
63	  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of
66	  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any
67	  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart
69	  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of
70	  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the
71	  source).
72	-/

8	/-!
9	# CHART-U(b): the openness of `chartLocus` (dat-b row B-4, the assembly)
10	
11	`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 (b-amendment) fixes the openness route of record as a
12	chain with THREE transports on top of the engine, and reserves `isOpen_chartLocus` as its
13	keystone.  This file is that assembly, and its central purpose is to make the *shape* of the
14	assembly checkable now that `chartLocus` exists (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean`), so that the
15	remaining obligation is a single named hypothesis rather than a fog.
16	
17	## What the route of record is, and which links are landed
18	
19	Reading the (b-amendment) against the tree at HEAD:
20	
21	| link | statement | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| (0) class-indexation | `isOpen_cechWitnessLocus` (`Pic0ChartLocusClass:123`) | **landed** (c9a) |
24	| engine | `datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` (`GluedSheafEngine:221`) | **landed** |
25	| dictionary | `subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`H1Locus:182`) | **landed** |
26	| RE-5 | `exists_fg_isNoetherianRing_baseChange_eq` (`DatumDescent:514`) | **landed** |
27	| datum openness | `isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` (`LocusOpen:80`) | **landed** |
28	| fibre-field | `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable` (`FibreField:157`) | **landed** |
29	| GAP-1 inverse | `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.invDatum` (`Pic0ChartShiftedDatum`) | **landed** |
30	| carrier/field translation | `isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField` | **landed** |
31	| twist collapse | `chartTwist_collapse` (`Pic0ChartTwistCollapse`) | **landed** |
32	| ~~GAP-1 mul~~ | ~~a datum for a *product*, on a common cover refinement~~ | **NOT NEEDED** |
33	| honesty over the étale carrier | `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` (`Pic0ChartHonest`) | **landed** |
34	| pointwise presentation | `IsChartDatumPresentation` (below) | **HALF landed** (see note) |
35	| `cechPicClass_inv` | the class law of `invDatum` | **NOT landed**, and off the path |
36	
37	(The engine is Noetherian-free; the GAP-1 inverse and the carrier/field translation landed
38	2026-07-28.)
39	
40	**The GAP-1 mul row is struck, and this paragraph is a correction of what stood here.**  It
41	used to say the residue was the shifted-datum presentation and that "producing it needs the
42	mul/tensor half of GAP-1, which needs a common refinement of two basic-open covers".  That is
43	false (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`): the twist is ONE `thetaFamily`, since
44	`sigmaFamily` *is* a `thetaFamily` and `thetaFamily` is multiplicative in its class, so Σ and
45	`θᵐ` fuse in `CechPic` over the fixed base before any datum is extracted; and
46	`exists_cechPicClass_eq` presents an arbitrary class, product or not, outright.
47	
48	**What genuinely remains, stated without under-pricing it** (this is the correction the
49	reviewer of I-0558 asked for).  Two things, and neither is bookkeeping:
50	
51	1. ~~**Honesty over a general affine base.**~~  **LANDED** (`Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean`).  This
52	   row read: `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass` takes an honest Čech class `c` over `B`
53	   as a *hypothesis*, and nothing supplies one, because the splitting theorem
54	   (`exists_splitting_of_picEt`) needs `[Field K]` — its engine is étale field-cofinality — and
55	   the only other plus-unit surjectivity is field-only too.  All of that is accurate about the
56	   tree and none of it matters: **a cover splits over its own carrier.**
57	   `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` gives `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (mk C E x) = unit C E.Carrier x`
58	   over an ARBITRARY affine base, because the map cofinality was being asked to produce is the
59	   *identity* `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier`.  This is exactly the (b-amendment)'s "over the étale
60	   carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is honest" step, so it was never a general-`A` obligation
61	   in the first place.
62	2. **The pointwise presentation itself** — now the ONLY residue.  `IsChartDatumPresentation` asks
63	   for ONE datum over
64	   `A` whose fibre predicate matches, at every residue field simultaneously, a split predicate
65	   whose splitting field `L` varies from point to point (`IsSplitWitness` quantifies `L`
66	   existentially *per point*).  Calling that "a `cechPicClass` base-change statement, not a
67	   construction" — as an earlier draft of this header did — prices a construction as
68	   bookkeeping, which is precisely the mis-pricing the twist-collapse retraction was written
69	   to correct one level up.
70	
71	Everything downstream of a presenting datum is landed.
72	
73	**UPDATE 2026-07-28 (`de63abac6`): the residue of row 2 is now HALF discharged, and the half
74	that fell was the one this paragraph did not expect.**
75	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationHalf.lean` proves the **forward** direction of
76	`IsChartDatumPresentation` from a hypothesis containing no witness, no `H¹` and no divisor:
77	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, which says only that the datum presents `μ` at every residue field *as
78	plus classes*.  The move is to take the splitting extension to be `κ(t)` **itself** — the datum's
79	witness divisor is already in the right class over `κ(t)` with vanishing `H¹`, so nothing needs
80	transporting.  That trivial splitting `L := K` had been recorded as unelaborable (memory I-0564);
81	it is one line since that record's partial retraction (see
82	`isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness` in `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`).
83	
84	What is still owed is the **converse**, and the per-point quantification of `L` this paragraph
85	warns about is exactly where it bites: one receives a witness over some `L_t` varying with `t`,
86	lying in `μ`'s class there rather than visibly in `D`'s at `κ(t)`.
87	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse` assembles the `↔` from the two halves, so a
88	lane closing this row faces one obligation instead of two.
89	
90	## The shape of this file
91	
92	`IsChartDatumPresentation` names exactly that residue as a hypothesis — a *per-field*
93	presentation of the twisted fibre class by a datum — and `isOpen_chartLocus_of_presentation`
94	derives the openness from it over an affine test.  This is the honest factorisation: the
95	theorem is real mathematics (it is the three transports plus the dictionary), and the
96	hypothesis is a single, precisely stated obligation.  (An earlier draft said the GAP-1
97	mul/tensor brick would discharge it; see the struck table row for why that was wrong.)
98	
99	Writing it the other way round — stating `isOpen_chartLocus` unconditionally with a `sorry`
100	— would hide the fact that the missing input is a *construction*, not a proof.
101	
102	**This file is sorry-free as of 2026-07-28.**  Its earlier single `sorry` (the carrier/field
103	translation) was not a mathematical gap: it was an artifact of taking the `Algebra A` /
104	`IsScalarTower k A` structures on `κ(t)` as explicit `alg`/`tow` *arguments*, which both made
105	the statement FALSE for some regradings — `HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its `Algebra` instance
106	inside `relCurveMap C B L`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different base-change map and a
107	different set — and forced every consumer to carry two dead parameters.  (No refuting
108	`A`, `alg` was exhibited, so the honest verdict is "wrong shape, false for some regradings",
109	not "no proof can exist"; recorded per I-0559.)  With the canonical
110	instances of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean` the whole translation is
111	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the carrier
112	identification `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is definitional.  The general lesson
113	is recorded on the `chart-u` roadmap node.
114	
115	## Main declarations
116	
117	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartDatumPresentation` — the residue, named.
118	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocus_eq_cechWitnessLocus_of_presentation` — the identification of
119	  `chartLocus` over an affine test with the landed class-indexed witness locus.  This is
120	  transports (0) and (iii) discharged.
121	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_presentation` — **the keystone, conditionally**:
122	  `chartLocus` is open over an affine test given the presentation.
123	-/
124	
125	set_option autoImplicit false
126	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
127	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
128	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
129	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
130	
131	universe u
132	
133	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
134	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
135	
136	open scoped TensorProduct
137	
138	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
139	
140	open AlgebraicJacobian
141	
142	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
143	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
144	
145	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
146	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
147	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
148	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
149	
150	noncomputable section
151	
152	/-! ## The residue of the chain, named -/
153	
154	variable (C π) in
155	/-- **The shifted-datum presentation hypothesis** — the one link of the CHART-U(b) route of
156	record that is not landed, stated exactly.
157	
158	Over an affine test `Spec A`, for a class `μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)` (in practice the
159	twisted family `chartTwist C m Z _ λ` restricted to the test), a presentation is a
160	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `A` whose fibre witness predicate at every residue field agrees
161	with the split witness predicate of `μ` at the corresponding point.
162	
163	Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:
164	
165	* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
166	  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
167	  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and
168	  a class-level identification, whereas a lane that can produce the pointwise agreement by any
169	  other route may use this theorem immediately;
170	* the split predicate is read at `Over.testPoint`, i.e. at the canonical residue-field point
171	  of the affine test, so no choice of affine chart enters;
172	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` / `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
173	  datum predicate needs are the **canonical** ones of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`.  An
174	  earlier draft of this file carried them as explicit `alg`/`tow` arguments; that was strictly
175	  worse — it made the statement false for some regradings (`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its
176	  `Algebra` instance inside `relCurveMap`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different set) as
177	  well as unusable. -/
178	def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
180	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
181	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
182	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
183	
184	/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`
185	
186	The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
187	`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
188	The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
189	(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
190	isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
191	into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/
192	
193	/-- **The residue-field comparison at a point of an affine test, as an algebra map.**
194	
195	`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
196	engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
197	prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in
198	the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
199	residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
200	
201	Proof: both sides are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`, and `Spec.map` is
202	injective on homs, so it suffices to compare after applying `Spec.map` — where the identity is
203	mathlib's `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField`. -/
204	lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
205	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
206	    algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
207	      = ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.comp
208	          (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
209	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
210	  have h : Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)
211	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField)
212	          ≫ (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv := by
213	    apply Spec.map_injective
214	    rw [Spec.map_preimage, Spec.map_comp]
215	    exact (Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField (.of A) t).symm
216	  rw [h]
217	  rfl
218	
219	/-- **The witness predicate at a scheme-residue field agrees with the one at the prime's
220	residue field, and the resulting locus is open.**
221	
222	`Over.testPointField t` is `(Spec A).residueField t` and the engine reads
223	`t.asIdeal.ResidueField`; `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them, and the witness predicate
224	transfers along any field extension in the `A`-tower
225	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:142`), in
226	particular along an isomorphism.
227	
228	Three points about the proof, each of which was a suspected wall and is not:
229	
230	* the **carrier identification** `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is *definitional*
231	  (`Scheme.Spec`'s carrier is `PrimeSpectrum` on the nose), so the two index sets need no
232	  transport and the two topologies agree by `rfl`.  The set equality below is therefore a
233	  pointwise `Iff`, not a homeomorphism argument;
234	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` and `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
235	  predicate needs are **already canonical** (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`,
236	  `Over.instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine`), so nothing has to be passed in as an
237	  argument.  An earlier draft of this file took `alg`/`tow` as explicit hypotheses and left
238	  the conclusion as a `sorry`; that was a statement-shape artifact, not a gap — and worse,
239	  the hypothesis form is *false for some regradings*, since an arbitrary `alg` need not be the
240	  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
241	* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
242	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
243	  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
244	  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
245	theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
246	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
247	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) :
248	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
249	      D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} := by
250	  -- The two loci are the SAME set of the SAME type: `↥(overSpec k A).left` is
251	  -- `PrimeSpectrum A` definitionally, so only the fibre field differs, and the predicate is
252	  -- invariant under the isomorphism between the two readings of it.
253	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
254	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)}
255	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum A |
256	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
257	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
258	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
259	                    D.cechPicClass
260	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
261	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
262	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
263	    refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
264	    -- the comparison iso as an algebra structure, and its tower over `A`
265	    letI : Algebra (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
266	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
267	      ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.toAlgebra
268	    haveI : IsScalarTower A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
269	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
270	      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors t)
271	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
272	      (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
273	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).symm
274	  rw [hset]
275	  exact D.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ
276	
277	/-! ## Transports (0) and (iii): the identification with the landed locus -/
278	
279	/-- **`chartLocus` over an affine test is the witness locus of a presenting datum.**
280	
281	This is transport (0) (the class-indexation, landed as `cechWitnessLocus`) composed with
282	transport (iii) (locality on the affine test, here trivial because the test *is* affine),
283	run against the presentation hypothesis.  The content is entirely the translation between
284	the two ways the tree indexes a fibre — by a point of the test object's space
285	(`Over.testPoint`, the `chartLocus` side) and by a prime of the test algebra
286	(`q.asIdeal.ResidueField`, the engine side).
287	
288	The translation is available precisely because `Over.testPointField` at a point of
289	`(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and `q.asIdeal.ResidueField` at the corresponding prime are
290	the same field up to the canonical `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the witness predicate is
291	invariant under field isomorphism over the base (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
292	applied to an isomorphism). -/
293	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing
294	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
295	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
296	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
297	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
298	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
299	  (hpres t).symm
300	
301	/-! ## The keystone, conditionally -/
302	
303	variable (C π) in
304	/-- **`isOpen_chartLocus`, given the shifted-datum presentation** (dat-b row B-4's keystone,
305	over an affine test).
306	
307	The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite
308	membership of `chartLocus` as the datum's witness predicate at the residue field of the
309	point (the presentation), then quote the landed datum-level openness
310	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
311	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.
312	
313	The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
314	(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
315	`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along
316	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`), and a set that is open in every member of an open cover is open.
317	That last step is `isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter`-style bookkeeping and needs no new
318	mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis
319	*per affine piece*, which is a statement about the general test and therefore belongs with
320	the honesty/presentation obligations named in the header table. -/
321	theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
322	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
323	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
324	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
325	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
326	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
327	  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of
328	  -- `Spec A`.  These carriers are the same type, so the presentation rewrites one into the
329	  -- other pointwise.
330	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
331	        IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)}
332	      = {t : (overSpec k A).left |
333	          D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} :=
334	    Set.ext fun t => mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing hpres t
335	  rw [hset]
336	  exact isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField hπ D
337	
338	end
339	
340	end AlgebraicGeometry

124	pullback regularity (`DivisorAdaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors`)
125	transports through the recorded `DivEq`. -/

127	    (hloc : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d)
128	    (y z : relCurve C R') (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
129	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y)
130	        z hz).hom (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)
131	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) := by
132	  classical
133	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hloc
134	  -- the away charts of `R'` at the pushed cover, and their immersions

148	        exact ⟨g i.down, ⟨i.down, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
149	      · rintro ⟨-, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩

151	    rw [hrange, ← Ideal.map_span, hg, Ideal.map_top]
152	  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_immersion_cover
153	    (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => relCurveMap C R'
154	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))
155	    (fun y' => exists_relCurveMap_base_eq C R'
156	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
157	      (fun i => Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) hspan' y')
158	    (relCurveMap C R R') d (fun i ζ => ?_) y z hz
159	  -- over the chart at `g i`: factor the composite through the certified localization

161	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) :=

180	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=

183	        ← RingHom.comp_assoc,

201	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : D.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
202	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
203	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
204	    (by
205	      intro a ha
206	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
207	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
208	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
209	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
210	          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
211	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
212	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
213	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
214	
215	/-- The product of the piece-local colengths. -/
216	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : D.index, A.colength j
217	
218	/-- The product of the overlap colengths over ordered index pairs. -/
219	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : D.index × D.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
220	
221	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer. -/
222	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
223	  LinearMap.pi
224	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
225	
226	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer. -/
227	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
228	  LinearMap.pi
229	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
230	
231	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`**, spelled as a kernel so the `FlatCokernel`
232	base-change keystone applies verbatim. -/
233	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
234	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
235	
236	/-- The equalizer description of `W(d)`. -/
237	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
238	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
239	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
240	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
241	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
242	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
243	
244	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
245	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
246	
247	/-! ### The certificate -/
248	
249	/-- **The colength certificate over a widened cover** — clauses (c1)–(c4) verbatim from
250	`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`.  Nothing is added and nothing is dropped: the widening
251	changes where the pieces LIVE, not what the certificate asserts. -/
252	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
253	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
254	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
255	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
256	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
257	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
258	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
259	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
260	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
261	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
262	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
263	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
264	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
265	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
266	  flat_coker_diff :
267	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))

  "body": "AN INDEX-WEAKENING IS ONLY AS WIDE AS THE EXPONENT (OR PARAMETER) ITS PRODUCER REACHES -- and the twist may be trivial exactly there.\n\nShape, from the ajcr-cert-r2 r8 review of ThetaTrivData (Picard/DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean). A layer was indexed by a datum no straddling cover inhabits (ChartTyping, I-0779). The fix replaced it with a genuinely chart-free datum and PROVED inhabitation -- but only at the parameter value a = 0, where the twisting unit is 1 and (verified by rfl) the 'twisted' module IS the pre-existing untwisted one. Two separate collapses were invisible to build/axiom/sorry checks:\n 1. the inhabited case computes an object the tree already had;\n 2. the same file's downstream declarations carry a cohomological hypothesis (Subsingleton H^1 of the twist) which AT a = 0 forces H^1(O_C) = 0, i.e. genus 0 -- so the produced index and a satisfiable hypothesis never co-exist on a curve of interest.\n\nTHE CHECK TO RUN, next time an index or hypothesis is weakened and inhabitation is proved at one parameter value: (a) instantiate the produced datum into the layer's own downstream statements and ask whether the resulting object is DEFEQ to something pre-existing; (b) take every OTHER hypothesis those statements carry and evaluate it AT that parameter value -- a bound stated for general 'a' can degenerate to a triviality assumption at the corner where your producer lives. Neither check is a sorry, a job count, or an axiom.\n\nGeneralises I-0779's lesson ('check inhabitation of an index before pricing anything stated over it') one step: check inhabitation AND check what the inhabited instance costs the rest of the statement.",

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
62	
63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section
75	
76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in
97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end
141	
142	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
69	-/

136	its chart locus together with the two properties the criterion needs.

138	This is `ChartFibrePresented` with its `W` field already discharged — it is `chartLocus`,
139	open unconditionally — so what a lane owes is precisely:

141	* `r`: the divisor family over the locus whose class is the given one.  This is the
142	  classifier `divRepClassifyZar` applied to the canonical-section family, i.e. CHART-U(c)'s
143	  construction;
144	* `sq`: that its chart value *is* the given class, which is the classifier's characterising
145	  property;
146	* `exists_factor`: that two points with the same class agree, i.e. the **relative form of
147	  DAT-C GAP-2** (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` in families).
148	
149	Stated as a `Prop` over an arbitrary presenting datum rather than as a structure carrying the
150	family, because the family is the classifier's output and this lane must not guess its shape:
151	the existential is over morphisms of schemes only. -/
152	def IsChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
153	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
154	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
155	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) : Prop :=
156	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
157	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) g)
158	
159	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: the residue above gives `IsChartUniv`, hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)`
160	pair, at *any* open of the divisor scheme.
161	
162	Two things are worth reading off the proof.  First, it goes through the criterion of
163	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` and then through the *composition* half
164	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` already landed in `Pic0ChartPair.lean` — so the two
165	halves of C9b compose exactly as the file headers predicted, with no seam.  Second, the open
166	`V` is arbitrary: restriction never has to be to the chart locus for `hf` to hold, because
167	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under precomposition with an open immersion.  The chart
168	locus is where the *unrestricted* statement becomes true, which is a statement about
169	`IsChartLocusFibre`, not about `V`. -/
170	theorem isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
171	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
172	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
173	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
174	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
175	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
176	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
177	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
178	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)

181	
182	/-- **`IsChartUniv` forces elementwise injectivity of the restricted chart.**
183	
184	The converse direction of the reduction, and the reason it is a reduction rather than a
185	restatement: a lane that obtains `IsChartUniv` has, for free, the injectivity statement that
186	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` is the hard half of.  So there is no route to `hf` that
187	avoids relative GAP-2 — the gate is real, and this file has moved it rather than removed it.
188	
189	Compare `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective`: that says the criterion cannot
190	be *satisfied* without injectivity; this says the goal cannot be *reached* without it. -/
191	theorem injective_of_isChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
192	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
193	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
194	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
195	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
196	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
197	    Function.Injective ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
198	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf h T

13	The Addendum-2 repair of the divisor-functor carrier (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`,
14	Addendum 2): the globally-certified `DivFam` is not a Zariski sheaf — the diagonal
15	divisor over `Γ(C \ pt)` is certifiable on a basic-open cover of the base but carries

29	  engine**: a locally certified system has regular pulled equations along the
30	  comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'` — regularity is germ-local, each germ

8	/-!
9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
14	CERT-Σ-gated.
15	
16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
19	
20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
23	
24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
29	
30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
31	
32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
37	
38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
42	
43	## Main declarations
44	
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
57	  this route.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
60	-/

112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
114	
115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
118	
119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
